texts.facts: 3. The brief facts of the case are that on 9.1.1998, the complainant along with Panch witness visited the premises of the respondent -accused No. 1. That, upon checking, the complainant decided to take sample of Tulsi Mix Gutkha and accordingly, informed the accused to analyze this sample before the Public Analyst. That, the complainant had purchased Tulsi Mix Guthkha and paid the amount. That, thereafter, the complainant obtained the signature of the accused in a receipt for receiving an amount. That, the said sample of Tulsi Mix Gutkha was taken after following due procedure of law in the presence of Panch witness, in three clean dry bottles, which were closed sufficiently tight to prevent leakage, evaporation. That, the complainant also obtained signatures of panchas in the panchnama, at the time of taking sample. That, the complainant had sent the samples to the Public Analyst for analysis. That, after analyzing the sample, the Public Analyst opined as "In contravention of provisions of rule 32(b) and 62 of PFA Rules, 1955, sample of "Tulsi Mix Gutkha" is misbranded under Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act 1954 as magnesium carbonate detected in the sample is not mentioned in the list of ingredients of the label and also contravenes the provisions of the rule 62 of PFA Rules, 1955." The complainant had obtained the permission of Local Health Authority and filed the complaint before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Surendranagar.
